In the 2026/27 tax year (6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027), adults aged 18 or over can pay up to £20,000 into ISAs. You can split this between cash ISAs, stocks and shares ISAs, innovative finance ISAs and a Lifetime ISA. The Lifetime ISA has its own limit of £4,000. Any unused allowance does not carry forward.

From 6 April 2027, investors under 65 will be capped at £12,000 a year in cash ISAs. The overall £20,000 allowance stays the same.

More detail is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

The ISA allowance for 2026/27 is £20,000 per adult aged 18 or over. The tax year runs from 6 April 2026 to 5 April 2027. You can split the allowance between cash ISAs, stocks and shares ISAs, innovative finance ISAs and a Lifetime ISA. The Lifetime ISA has its own limit of £4,000. Unused allowance does not carry forward.

Changes start from 6 April 2027. Investors under 65 will then be capped at £12,000 a year into cash ISAs. The overall £20,000 allowance stays the same.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

I can't confirm that from our documents. They only cover ISAs for adults aged 18 or over, with an allowance of £20,000 in the 2026/27 tax year. They also say a Lifetime ISA can be opened by anyone aged 18 to 39. They don't say whether a 17-year-old can open an ISA with us.

Please raise this with an adviser, or ask the switchboard. You can read the ISA guide at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

You can pay up to £4,000 a year into a Lifetime ISA. That counts towards the £20,000 overall ISA allowance. The government adds a 25% bonus of up to £1,000 a year.

You can open a Lifetime ISA if you're aged 18 to 39. Withdrawals for any reason other than the following incur a 25% government charge:
- buying a first home costing £450,000 or less, once the account has been open for at least 12 months
- age 60 or over
- terminal illness with less than 12 months to live

More detail is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

At 42 you're over the age limit. A Lifetime ISA can be opened by anyone aged 18 to 39.

The documents don't say whether another option would suit you. For that, please raise it with your adviser. More detail is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

The ISA guide lists these changes from 6 April 2027:

- Investors under 65 can pay at most £12,000 a tax year into cash ISAs. The overall £20,000 allowance is unchanged. The remainder can still go into stocks and shares or innovative finance ISAs. Investors aged 65 and over keep a £20,000 cash ISA limit.
- Transfers from stocks and shares or innovative finance ISAs into cash ISAs will no longer be permitted.
- A charge will apply to interest paid on cash held inside a stocks and shares or innovative finance ISA.
- Money already in cash ISAs is not affected by the cap.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

I can't say what you should do about your own ISAs. Please raise that with your adviser.

According to our ISA guide, the cap probably doesn't apply to you. From 6 April 2027, the cash ISA cap is £12,000 a year for investors under 65. Investors aged 65 and over keep a £20,000 cash ISA limit. Money already in cash ISAs isn't affected by the cap.

The same changes also stop transfers from stocks and shares or innovative finance ISAs into cash ISAs. The guide also says a charge will apply to interest paid on cash held inside those ISAs. If you want advice on what to do with your own money, I can pass you to an adviser.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

Under HM Revenue & Customs' guidelines, transfers between cash ISAs should take no longer than 15 working days. Other ISA transfers should take no longer than 30 calendar days. Re-registering holdings in specie (moving them as they are) can take longer if fund managers are slow to respond.

The new provider starts the transfer. Don't withdraw the money yourself, because the ISA keeps its tax status only if the transfer goes through the new provider's transfer process. We don't charge for transfers in or out.

More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

Yes. Our stocks and shares ISA is flexible. You can replace money you withdraw in the same tax year without using more of your allowance.

The documents don't say anything more about this, such as any conditions. For questions about your own circumstances, please raise them with your adviser. You can read more in the ISAs guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

Yes, in part. A surviving spouse or civil partner gets an additional permitted subscription equal to the value of the deceased's ISAs. This is on top of their own allowance. They get it whether or not they inherit the investments themselves.

The ISA also stays tax-free as a continuing account of a deceased investor for up to three years while the estate is administered. ISAs still count as part of your estate for inheritance tax.

The documents don't cover how to claim this or what applies in your own situation. Please raise those with your adviser. More detail is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

The annual allowance is £60,000. If the total paid into your pensions in a tax year exceeds it, an annual allowance charge is normally due. That total includes employer contributions and the value of any defined benefit accrual.

- **High earners:** the allowance tapers down to a minimum of £10,000.
- **Carry forward:** you can carry forward unused allowance from the previous three tax years, provided you were a member of a registered pension scheme in those years.
- **Money purchase annual allowance:** once you have taken taxable income flexibly from a defined contribution pension, a £10,000 money purchase annual allowance applies to further defined contribution contributions.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

I can't advise on how this applies to your own situation. For that, please speak to an adviser.

Yes, you can still pay into a defined contribution pension after taking income through drawdown, but a lower limit applies. Once you've taken taxable income flexibly from a defined contribution pension, the money purchase annual allowance of £10,000 applies to further defined contribution contributions.

The documents I have don't say whether this affects your own situation. Please raise that with your adviser. More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

Normally, you can take up to 25% of a pension tax free. This is subject to the lump sum allowance of £268,275 across all your pensions. Lump sums above that allowance are taxed at your marginal rate.

I can't advise on whether or how much you should take. If you'd like advice on that, I can pass you to an adviser. More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

You can draw from a defined contribution pension from age 55. This rises to 57 from 6 April 2028. The options are flexi-access drawdown, buying an annuity, taking lump sums, or a combination. Each has different tax consequences.

When you apply to access a pension, we will refer you to Pension Wise and offer to book a free guidance appointment for you. We won't do this if you have already had one or have received regulated advice.

I can't advise on which option suits you. More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

Yes. If the transfer value is more than £30,000, the law requires you to take appropriate independent advice before the transfer can proceed. The advice must come from a firm with Financial Conduct Authority permission to advise on pension transfers. Fernhill Wealth holds that permission.

The Financial Conduct Authority expects advisers to start from the assumption that a transfer won't be suitable. Fernhill recommends one only where it can show the transfer is clearly in your interest. The documents don't say what applies to transfer values of £30,000 or less. If that's your situation, please raise it with your adviser.

Under the current rules, the documents don't say that pensions are subject to inheritance tax. They do say this changes from 6 April 2027:

- From 6 April 2027, most unused pension funds and death benefits will be included in the value of your estate for inheritance tax.
- Benefits passing to a spouse or civil partner, or to a registered charity, remain exempt.
- Dependants' scheme pensions and death-in-service benefits are outside the new rules.

Separately from inheritance tax, if you die before age 75, benefits are normally paid free of income tax, within the lump sum and death benefit allowance of £1,073,100. If you die at or after 75, the recipient pays income tax at their marginal rate.

I can't say how this applies to your own situation. Please raise that with your adviser. Our financial planning service also covers inheritance tax and estate planning.

Yes, you can still get tax relief. Your own contributions receive tax relief up to 100% of your relevant UK earnings in the tax year, or £3,600 gross if your earnings are lower. With no earnings, the £3,600 gross figure is the one that applies. Basic-rate relief is added to the pension automatically.

I can't say whether you should pay in, or how much. That's a question for an adviser. I can pass it to one if you'd like. More detail is on the pensions guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

Yes. Our pensions guide says unused annual allowance from the previous three tax years can be carried forward, provided you were a member of a registered pension scheme in those years.

The annual allowance is £60,000. For high earners it tapers down to a minimum of £10,000. The documents don't say how much you could carry forward in your own case. Please raise that with your adviser. The guide is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/pensions/

Our standard rates for financial planning are:

- **Full financial plan:** £2,400, plus VAT where it applies. It covers a review of your whole financial position, a written plan with recommendations, and a meeting to go through it.
- **One-off advice on a single topic:** £1,200, plus VAT where it applies. An example is how to use allowances before the end of the tax year.

We are paid by fees agreed with you in advance, and we don't receive commission from product providers. We confirm all fees in writing in your client agreement and services and costs disclosure before any work starts. You can see them on the Fees and Charges page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

Ongoing advice costs 0.75% a year of the assets under advice, collected monthly from your accounts. It covers your annual review meeting, access to your adviser throughout the year, rebalancing recommendations and the quarterly reports.

If you also have discretionary investment management, that fee applies as well. Your client agreement sets out the combined cost. Your annual costs and charges statement shows it in pounds.

More details are on the fees and charges page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

The documents don't give a fee figure for a £2m portfolio. They give a tiered annual management fee, and VAT is added to it:

- 0.60% a year on the first £1,000,000.
- 0.45% a year on the portion between £1,000,000 and £3,000,000.
- 0.30% a year on the portion above £3,000,000.

If we provide both ongoing advice and discretionary management, both fees apply. The combined cost is set out in your client agreement and shown in pounds in your annual costs and charges statement.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

It depends on the account type:

- **Model portfolios:** There are no dealing charges. That includes when holdings are sold to pay a withdrawal or to close an account.
- **Advisory accounts:** Individual share trades cost £12.50 each.

Custody of your assets by our custodian costs 0.15% a year. More details are at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

It depends on the service:

- Advice that leads to us arranging a product or investment for you is exempt from VAT.
- Stand-alone advice and discretionary investment management are subject to VAT at the standard rate.

Your client agreement states which of your fees carry VAT. More detail is on the fees and charges page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

No. We're paid by fees agreed with you in advance, and we don't receive commission from product providers. Your client agreement and services and costs disclosure confirm all fees in writing before any work starts.

You can see the standard rates on our Fees and Charges page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

Our discretionary investment management service is designed for portfolios of £250,000 or more. Financial planning is available at any level of wealth.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

No, there's no charge for closing an account or for transferring out. On our model portfolios, there are no dealing charges if holdings have to be sold.

Fund charges continue to be deducted within the funds until the holdings are transferred or sold.

More detail is on the closing or transferring page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/closing-or-transferring/

The funds we invest in have their own charges on top of our fee. The fund managers set these, and they're deducted within the fund. Across our model portfolios, the average ongoing fund charge was 0.21% a year at 30 June 2026.

Each April we send every client a statement showing all the charges paid in the previous year, in pounds. It covers our fees, custody, dealing and fund charges. More detail is on the Fees and charges page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/fees-and-charges/

You can complain by letter, telephone, email or in person, and you can raise it with anyone in the firm. You can also contact the Client Resolution team directly:
- Email: complaints@fernhillwealth.example
- Telephone: 0117 496 0355, 09:00 to 17:30 on working days
- Post: Client Resolution, Fernhill Wealth, Fernhill House, 22 Harbourside Walk, Bristol, BS1 5XY

Making a complaint is free and won't affect the service you receive. If someone is complaining for you, we need your written permission before we can discuss your affairs with them.

**What happens next**
- If we can resolve it within three working days, we confirm this in a summary resolution letter.
- Otherwise we acknowledge your complaint in writing within five working days and tell you who is handling it.
- We then investigate, and we may contact you for more information.
- We finish with a final response letter.
- If the investigation can't be completed within eight weeks, we write to explain the delay.

More detail is on the complaints page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/complaints/

The documents give these timings:

- If we can resolve the complaint within three working days, we confirm it in a summary resolution letter.
- Otherwise, we acknowledge it in writing within five working days and tell you who is handling it.
- If the investigation can't be completed within eight weeks of receiving your complaint, we write to explain the delay and when we expect to respond. We also tell you that you can go to the Financial Ombudsman Service without waiting.

If you're unhappy with our final response, or if eight weeks pass without one, you can refer the matter to the Financial Ombudsman Service free of charge. You must do this within six months of the date of our final response.

More detail is on our complaints page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/complaints/

If you're unhappy with our final response, you can refer the matter to the Financial Ombudsman Service. This is free. You must do it within six months of the date of our final response.

- Telephone: 0800 023 4567, or 0300 123 9123
- Website: www.financial-ombudsman.org.uk
- Post: Financial Ombudsman Service, Exchange Tower, London, E14 9SR

You can also contact our Client Resolution team at complaints@fernhillwealth.example or on 0117 496 0355, 09:00 to 17:30 on working days.

The Financial Ombudsman Service's telephone numbers are 0800 023 4567 and 0300 123 9123.

You can refer a complaint to them free of charge if you're unhappy with our final response, or if eight weeks pass without one. You must do so within six months of the date of our final response.

Four years on may not be too late. The Ombudsman can normally consider a complaint made within six years of the event. It can also consider one made within three years of when you became aware, or ought reasonably to have become aware, that you had cause to complain. Whichever of those is later applies.

If you're unsure whether your complaint is in time, contact us anyway. You can find more on the complaints page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/complaints/

Use the "Forgotten password" link on the login page. A reset link will be emailed to the address we hold, and it's valid for 30 minutes.

If your account is locked, it stays locked for 30 minutes after five incorrect attempts. If you're still locked out after that, call the portal access helpline on 0117 496 0233. It's open 09:00 to 17:30 on working days.

More information: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/portal/

Five incorrect login attempts lock your account for 30 minutes. If you're still locked out after that, call the portal access helpline on 0117 496 0233. It's open 09:00 to 17:30 on working days.

Other options, depending on the cause:
- **Forgotten password:** use the Forgotten password link on the login page. A reset link is emailed to the address we hold and is valid for 30 minutes.
- **No verification code:** check that your phone has signal, or use the backup codes issued when you set up two-step verification.
- **Changed phone number:** call the helpline so we can re-register your device. We will ask you to confirm your identity.

More detail is on the client portal support page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/portal/

No, two-step verification can't be switched off. You log in with your email address, your password and a six-digit code. The code comes from your authenticator app or is sent by text message.

You can read more on the client portal page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/portal/

You can see transactions for the last seven years in the client portal.

More details are on the portal page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/portal/

You can change your address in the client portal under My Details, or by secure message.

More details are on the client support page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/

To change your name after marriage, we need a certified copy of your marriage or civil partnership certificate. The documents don't say whether you also need to send your birth certificate in this case. The birth certificate is listed only alongside a divorce or dissolution final order. A deed poll is also accepted.

The documents don't say how to send these in. Your adviser can tell you. More details are at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/

For a general investment account or ISA:

- **Cash already available:** we pay within five working days of your instruction.
- **Holdings have to be sold first:** sales normally settle within two working days of dealing. We then pay within five working days of settlement.

Pension withdrawals depend on your age and the type of pension, and tax may be payable. The Pensions page explains the options.

Valuation reports are issued quarterly. They come within 15 working days of the end of March, June, September and December, and they are published to the client portal.

You can also ask your adviser's team for a valuation as at any date. It is normally available within two working days.

To change the bank account we pay withdrawals to, you need to give us two things:
- a signed instruction
- a recent statement for the new account that shows your name

We then confirm the change with you by telephone, on the number we hold, before it takes effect.

Withdrawals are only paid to a bank account in your name that we have verified in this way. The documents I have don't say where to send the instruction and statement. Please check the client support page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/

Yes. Paper copies by post can be arranged at no extra charge. Ask your adviser's team to set it up.

All documents are still published to the portal as well.

Yes. Interest is paid on cash balances at the rates shown on the portal. We keep a margin of 0.25% a year between the rate we receive and the rate we pay. This is disclosed in your client agreement.

Interest on cash outside an ISA or pension is taxable. It is reported on your annual consolidated tax certificate. From 6 April 2027 a charge will also apply to interest paid on cash held inside a stocks and shares ISA. The ISA guide explains this.

More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/cash-and-dealing/

Regular income is paid on the 25th of the month to your verified bank account. You can take it monthly, quarterly or annually from a general investment account or ISA.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/cash-and-dealing/

The smallest monthly direct debit you can set up is £250. Regular contributions are invested in line with your agreed portfolio on the next dealing day after we receive them.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/cash-and-dealing/

Fund sales are placed at the fund's next valuation point and settle within four working days. Money from a sale can be paid out once settlement has taken place. For a Monday sale, that means settlement within four working days of dealing.

The documents don't say when the money will reach your bank account after settlement. If you want it withdrawn, that is a separate instruction. Cash that is already available is paid within five working days of your instruction. Details are on the Cash and dealing page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/cash-and-dealing/

The annual exempt amount for capital gains tax is £3,000. It applies to gains on investments sold in a general investment account.

Gains above that amount on shares and funds are taxed at 18% or 24%, depending on your total taxable income. You can set losses against gains in the same year. You can also carry them forward if you report them to HMRC.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/tax/

I can't advise on how this applies to your own situation. If you'd like that, I can pass you to an adviser.

Outside an ISA, dividends are tax-free up to the dividend allowance of £500 a year. Above that, they're taxed at:
- 10.75% for basic-rate taxpayers
- 35.75% for higher-rate taxpayers
- 39.35% for additional-rate taxpayers

This applies to investments held outside an ISA or pension in the 2026/27 tax year. It is general information, not personal advice. Our tax guide is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/tax/

The consolidated tax certificate is published to the portal by the end of May each year. It shows dividends, interest and tax deducted for the tax year.

More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/tax/

No, we don't complete tax returns. Your adviser can introduce you to an accountant if you need one.

We do provide documents to help with your return:
- A consolidated tax certificate, published to the portal by the end of May each year. It shows dividends, interest and tax deducted for the tax year.
- A capital gains report. It shows realised gains and losses and the figures needed for the capital gains pages of a tax return.

More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/tax/

A Bed and ISA means selling holdings in a general investment account and buying them back within an ISA. It uses your ISA allowance and may realise a capital gain.

On our model portfolios there is no dealing charge for a Bed and ISA. The documents I have don't say what it costs outside model portfolios. Please ask your adviser about that.

More information: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/tax/

Pension transfers typically take four to eight weeks. The receiving provider starts the transfer. Their scheme carries out the checks required by the pension transfer regulations. It may require you to take guidance from MoneyHelper if those checks raise an amber flag.

We keep you informed through the portal at each stage. More detail is on the Closing or Transferring page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/closing-or-transferring/

The new provider starts the transfer. Once we receive their request, we process it. You shouldn't withdraw the money yourself, because the ISA keeps its tax status only if the transfer goes through the new provider's transfer process.

Under HM Revenue & Customs' guidelines, cash ISA transfers should take no longer than 15 working days. Other ISA transfers should take no longer than 30 calendar days. Re-registering holdings in specie can take longer where fund managers are slow to respond. We don't charge for transfers in or out.

Yes. Your documents stay available in the portal for seven years after the account closes. You can request paper copies at any time at no charge.

More details are on the closing or transferring page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/client-support/closing-or-transferring/

**Discretionary management:** You agree an investment mandate and risk level with us. Our investment managers then make the day-to-day decisions within that mandate.

**Advisory management:** We recommend changes, and you decide whether to make each one.

Which one suits you depends on how involved you want to be in individual decisions. Your adviser will talk through both with you, and the choice is recorded in your suitability report. More detail is on the investment management page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/investment-management/

Portfolios are managed to one of seven risk profiles. Profile 1 is the lowest risk, mainly cash and short-dated bonds. Profile 7 is the highest risk, almost entirely equities.

You agree your profile with your adviser. This uses a questionnaire and a conversation about your capacity for loss. It is reviewed at every annual review. Your adviser can tell you which profile to choose.

More information: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/investment-management/

For a discretionary portfolio, yes. If its value falls by 10% or more since the start of a quarterly reporting period, "we tell you by the end of the working day on which it happens, as the rules require."

You also get a quarterly valuation report on the client portal. It is published within 15 working days of each quarter end. The documents don't say how a fall is communicated, or what happens with non-discretionary portfolios. Your investment manager can answer those questions.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/investment-management/

No. Our independent custodian holds your investments through its nominee company, and legal title is registered in the nominee's name. You remain the beneficial owner.

Your holdings are identified to you in the custodian's records. They are kept separate from the firm's and the custodian's own assets under the Financial Conduct Authority's client assets rules. If the firm or the custodian failed and there was a shortfall, the Financial Services Compensation Scheme may cover eligible claims up to £85,000 per person.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/investment-management/

Yes. Each risk profile comes in a responsible version. It excludes companies that get more than 10% of their revenue from tobacco, controversial weapons or thermal coal. It also applies our published responsible investment policy when selecting funds.

Fees are the same as for the standard portfolios. These portfolios do not carry a sustainability label under the FCA's Sustainability Disclosure Requirements. The Responsible Investment Policy is available on request and on the website: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/investment-management/

I can't say whether this option is right for you. Please raise that with an adviser.

Yes, Fernhill Wealth is covered by the Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS).

- **Investment business:** If we were unable to meet our obligations, eligible clients could claim up to £85,000 per person.
- **Cash:** Cash held with our deposit-taking partner banks is protected up to £120,000 per person, per banking licence. Brands within the same banking group may share one licence.

Details are on the FSCS website. More information is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/about-us/

Cash held with our deposit-taking partner banks is protected up to £120,000 per person, per banking licence. Brands within the same banking group may share one licence.

Separately, if Fernhill Wealth couldn't meet its obligations, eligible clients could claim up to £85,000 per person for investment business. The FSCS website has more details.

We have six offices across England and Scotland: Bristol (head office), London, Manchester, Edinburgh, Leeds and Birmingham. Advisers at every office are also available for telephone and video meetings.

More details are at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/contact-us/

Yes. Fernhill Wealth is a trading name of Fernhill Wealth Limited, which is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority. You can check our authorisation on the Financial Services Register at register.fca.org.uk.

The company is registered in England and Wales. Its registered office is Fernhill House, 22 Harbourside Walk, Bristol, BS1 5XY.

Fernhill Wealth gives independent advice. We consider products from across the whole market and aren't restricted to any provider's range.

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/services/financial-planning/

The first meeting is a free introductory appointment. It lasts about 45 minutes and carries no obligation. You can have it at any of our six offices, by telephone or by video call. We explain how we work, what our services cost, and whether we think we can help. You don't need to bring anything. If you both decide to go ahead, we send a client agreement setting out the agreed work and fees before anything is charged.

If you go on to financial planning, the first step is a discovery meeting. It usually lasts 90 minutes. We gather information about your circumstances, goals and attitude to risk. For that meeting it helps to bring recent statements for any pensions, investments, mortgages and insurance policies. Bring an idea of your income and regular outgoings too.

You can book through the Book an Appointment page or by calling 0808 157 0450.

In our financial planning service, the written plan is presented at a second meeting. That meeting is usually three to four weeks after the discovery meeting.
